paper_title: High-Efficiency Thermal-Annealing-Free Organic Solar Cells Based on an Asymmetric Acceptor with Improved Thermal and Air Stability

knowledge_points.content: TB-4Cl is an asymmetric small molecule acceptor (SMA) featuring an A-D1A'D2-A framework and an asymmetric ladder-type core.
knowledge_points.evidence: In this work, a novel asymmetric molecule TB-4Cl was designed and synthesized... designed a new asymmetric acceptor TB-4Cl with an A-D1A'D2-A structure.

knowledge_points.content: Organic solar cells based on the PM6:TB-4Cl blend achieved a power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 14.67% without the use of thermal annealing (TA-free).
knowledge_points.evidence: Without thermal annealing, devices based on PM6:TB-4Cl achieved a higher efficiency of 14.67%.

knowledge_points.content: TB-4Cl exhibits a dipole moment of 1.98 Debye, which is significantly higher than the 1.07 Debye observed for the symmetric acceptor Y6, leading to enhanced intermolecular dipole-dipole interactions.
knowledge_points.evidence: Quantum chemical computations revealed that TB-4Cl has a larger dipole moment of 1.98 Debye than that of Y6 (1.07 Debye), which can induce a stronger intermolecular interaction.

knowledge_points.content: Unencapsulated inverted devices based on PM6:TB-4Cl retain 75% of their initial PCE after heating at 100 °C in nitrogen for 110 hours, outperforming PM6:Y6 devices which retain only 60%.
knowledge_points.evidence: PM6:TB-4Cl-based devices exhibited improved thermal and air stability, evidenced by retaining around 75% (TB-4Cl) and 60% (Y6) after being heated at 100 °C in nitrogen for 110 h.

knowledge_points.content: PM6:TB-4Cl-based solar cells show superior air stability over PM6:Y6, maintaining 65% of initial efficiency after 92 hours in air (60-70% humidity) compared to 50% for Y6.
knowledge_points.evidence: 65% (TB-4Cl) and 50% (Y6) in air for 92 h... storage time in air (20-30 °C, 60-70% humidity).

knowledge_points.content: DFT calculations at the wb97xd/6-31g** level indicate that TB-4Cl has a planar structure with small dihedral angles (0.74° and 0.61°), which facilitates π-π packing and electron mobility.
knowledge_points.evidence: The density functional theory (DFT) calculations at wb97xd/6.31g** were conducted to optimize molecular conformation... The dihedral angles of 0.74° and 0.61° indicate that TB-4Cl has a planar structure.

knowledge_points.content: The HOMO and LUMO energy levels of TB-4Cl are -5.7 eV and -4.1 eV, respectively, which are well-matched with the polymer donor PM6 (-5.47 eV/-3.67 eV).
knowledge_points.evidence: Figure 3a shows the HOMO/LUMO energy levels of TB-4Cl (-5.7/-4.1 eV), which match well with those of PM6 (-5.47/-3.67 eV).

knowledge_points.content: TB-4Cl-based devices are insensitive to thermal annealing, showing nearly identical PCE values before and after treatment (e.g., 14.67% TA-free vs. 14.56% with TA for PM6:TB-4Cl).
knowledge_points.evidence: Impressively, all of the devices showed a negligible difference in power conversion efficiency (PCE) before and after thermal-annealing treatment... 14.67 (14.58 ± 0.15) [free] and 14.56 (14.53 ± 0.08) [100 C].

knowledge_points.content: GIWAXS analysis confirms that TB-4Cl molecules in binary blend films adopt a face-on orientation, evidenced by a strong π-π stacking peak in the out-of-plane direction at q = 1.70 Å⁻¹ (d = 3.70 Å).
knowledge_points.evidence: In the OOP direction, there are the same qz = 1.70 Å (d = 3.70 Å), which is assigned to intermolecular π-π stacking of TB-4Cl, verifying that molecules in binary blend films tend to form a face-on orientation.

knowledge_points.content: The TA-free PM6:TB-4Cl devices exhibit balanced charge transport with an electron mobility of 5.76 × 10⁻⁴ cm² V⁻¹ s⁻¹ and a hole mobility of 4.29 × 10⁻⁴ cm² V⁻¹ s⁻¹.
knowledge_points.evidence: electron mobility and hole mobility are... 5.76 × 10⁻⁴ / 4.29 × 10⁻⁴ cm² V⁻¹ s⁻¹ for PM6:TB-4Cl (TA-free).

knowledge_points.content: TB-4Cl exhibits a 75 nm red shift in its absorption peak from solution (732 nm) to film (807 nm), indicating significant intermolecular π-π packing in the solid state.
knowledge_points.evidence: the peak of absorbance increases from 732 nm in solution to 807 nm in film. A 75 nm red shift confirms that TB-4Cl has a strong molecular π-π packing.

knowledge_points.content: TB-4Cl-based films without thermal annealing exhibit slightly larger phase separation than annealed films, which is theorized to reduce the donor/acceptor interface area and contribute to higher open-circuit voltage (Voc).
knowledge_points.evidence: TB-4Cl-based films with TA-free exhibit a slightly larger phase separation than that of TA-processed films. The slightly larger phase separation can lessen the D/A interface area, thus leading to the improvement of Voc.
